autocomplete.useWhen: Use Autocomplete when suggestions accelerate text entry but a value outside the suggestion set remains valid.
autocomplete.avoidWhen: Use Combobox or Select when the submitted value must match an authoritative option identifier.
keyboard: Typing changes the free-text value and filters suggestions.
Arrow Down and Arrow Up move the active suggestion.
Enter accepts the active suggestion; Escape dismisses suggestions without clearing text.
a11yNotes: The editable value remains the source of truth even when no suggestion matches.
The combobox exposes expansion, controls, autocomplete mode, and active descendant.
Loading, empty, and error result states remain perceivable without moving focus.
autocomplete.lifecycleRationale: The free-text and suggestion state contract remains beta while async replacement and assistive-technology evidence are completed.
knownLimitations: Applications must validate async suggestion replacement and announcement timing with their own data source.
Manual screen-reader evidence is required before promotion to stable.

bar-chart.useWhen: Use Bar Chart to compare a small set of categorical values where a common baseline makes differences meaningful.
bar-chart.avoidWhen: Use Line Chart for ordered trends and a table when exact values or many categories dominate the task.
keyboard: Tab reaches the source-data toggle, then the single roving data mark.
Arrow Left and Arrow Right move between marks and reverse in RTL.
Home and End move to the first and last mark; Enter or Space discloses its value.
a11yNotes: The chart has a specific title and a keyboard-operable data representation.
A semantic source-data table exposes the same labels and values.
Color is supplemented by labels, focus treatment, and the value detail.
bar-chart.lifecycleRationale: The accessible mark-navigation and source-table contract remains beta while chart scale and manual assistive-technology evidence mature.
knownLimitations: The primitive does not yet provide grouped or stacked series, axes customization, or large-series virtualization.
Consumers must verify value formatting and mark density with production data.

bottom-sheet.useWhen: Use Bottom Sheet for a focused modal task that must remain reachable on narrow touch layouts.
bottom-sheet.avoidWhen: Use Dialog for viewport-independent modal work and Drawer for a side-oriented workflow.
keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside the open modal surface.
Escape closes the topmost dismissible sheet.
Focus returns to the element that opened the sheet.
a11yNotes: The surface exposes modal dialog semantics and a visible title.
Nested overlays register ownership so Escape and focus restoration affect only the top layer.
Body scrolling is restored after the last modal layer closes.
bottom-sheet.lifecycleRationale: The responsive modal geometry and nested-overlay behavior remain beta until cross-device and manual assistive-technology evidence is complete.
knownLimitations: There is no public imperative overlay service; open state is currently template-owned.
Applications must verify virtual-keyboard and safe-area behavior on their supported mobile devices.

color-picker.useWhen: Use Color Picker when users need a validated color value plus visual hue, saturation, lightness, and preview controls.
color-picker.avoidWhen: Use a fixed Select or Radio Group when the product accepts only a small semantic palette.
keyboard: Enter or Space opens the picker and Escape closes it.
Arrow keys adjust the focused hue, saturation, or lightness control.
Tab follows the visible controls and Apply commits the draft color.
a11yNotes: Every visual color axis has a named keyboard-operable control and numeric value.
The text value remains visible so color is not the only representation.
Invalid color text is announced without silently replacing the committed value.
color-picker.lifecycleRationale: The color model and picker interaction remain beta while input-format scope and manual assistive-technology evidence are finalized.
knownLimitations: The public value contract is limited to documented CSS color formats and is not a color-management system.
Consumers requiring constrained brand colors should provide a semantic palette instead of unrestricted input.

combobox.useWhen: Use Combobox when typing should filter options and the committed value must come from an authoritative list.
combobox.avoidWhen: Use Autocomplete when unmatched free text is valid, or Select when filtering adds no value.
keyboard: Typing filters options; Arrow Down and Arrow Up move the active option.
Enter commits the active option.
Escape closes the popup without inventing or changing a value.
a11yNotes: The input exposes combobox, expanded, controls, and active-descendant state.
A committed value resolves back to its option label after asynchronous options arrive.
Loading, empty, and error option states are announced without stealing focus.
combobox.lifecycleRationale: The constrained async-selection contract remains beta while late option hydration and assistive-technology evidence are completed.
knownLimitations: Consumers must provide stable option identity across asynchronous refreshes.
Manual screen-reader validation is required for application-specific loading and error copy.

command-palette.useWhen: Use Command Palette for a searchable, temporary launcher over a bounded set of application commands.
command-palette.avoidWhen: Use Menu for a small contextual action set and Global Search for content discovery with a results page.
keyboard: Arrow Down and Arrow Up move through enabled results.
Enter invokes the active command.
Escape closes the palette and restores focus to its opener.
a11yNotes: The modal surface has a visible heading and labelled combobox/listbox relationship.
The active result is exposed through aria-activedescendant.
Empty results and command execution remain perceivable without adding duplicate tab stops.
command-palette.lifecycleRationale: The command registration and modal search contract remains beta while scale limits and manual assistive-technology evidence are established.
knownLimitations: The component does not provide a global command registry or application keyboard-shortcut service.
Consumers own command authorization, asynchronous execution, and route-transition error handling.

data-grid.useWhen: Use Data Grid for interactive tabular data that needs stable row identity, sorting, selection, controlled loading, or fixed-height row virtualization.
data-grid.avoidWhen: Use a semantic table for static content, and do not enable virtual mode for variable-height or expandable detail rows.
keyboard: Arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up, and Page Down move the single roving grid focus.
Enter or F2 enters the focused cell action; Escape returns to grid navigation.
Tab enters or leaves the grid without tabbing through every cell.
a11yNotes: Rows, columns, sort direction, selection, and virtual positions are exposed through grid semantics.
Every source occurrence requires a stable unique rowIdentity result.
Pinned columns preserve logical reading and focus order in LTR and RTL.
data-grid.lifecycleRationale: The grid remains beta because server data, virtualization, pinning, and consumer harness evidence must mature together before API freeze.
knownLimitations: Virtual mode currently requires measurable fixed-height rows and rejects expandable detail rows.
Grouping, variable-height rows, and column virtualization are not part of the current public contract.

data-table.useWhen: Use Data Table as the Data Grid alias when product language prefers table while retaining the same interactive contract.
data-table.avoidWhen: Use a native table for read-only content that does not need grid navigation, selection, or virtualization.
keyboard: Arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up, and Page Down move the single roving grid focus.
Enter or F2 enters a cell action; Escape restores grid navigation.
Tab enters or leaves the table as one composite widget.
a11yNotes: Data Table deliberately exposes grid semantics because it is an alias of Data Grid.
Stable row identity is mandatory across sorting, filtering, and paging.
Interactive cell content participates in managed action mode rather than the page tab sequence.
data-table.lifecycleRationale: The alias follows the beta lifecycle and evidence requirements of the canonical Data Grid contract.
knownLimitations: All Data Grid virtualization and grouping limitations also apply to Data Table.
The alias must not be treated as a separate native-table implementation.

date-picker.useWhen: Use Date Picker for one locale-formatted plain date while preserving an ISO YYYY-MM-DD domain value.
date-picker.avoidWhen: Use Date Range Picker for an interval and a native date input only when platform behavior is the explicit requirement.
keyboard: Enter or Space opens the calendar and Escape closes it.
Arrow keys move by day; Home and End move within the week.
Page Up and Page Down move by month; Enter or Space selects the focused date.
a11yNotes: The trigger exposes dialog expansion and the calendar uses grid semantics.
Month changes, disabled dates, selected date, and today remain perceivable.
Locale formatting never changes the ISO plain-date form value.
date-picker.lifecycleRationale: The plain-date contract remains beta while locale, boundary, hydration, and manual screen-reader evidence are completed.
knownLimitations: Timezone conversion and date-time instants remain application concerns.
Consumers must provide deterministic today when server and client clocks can differ.

date-range-picker.useWhen: Use Date Range Picker when users must choose an ordered inclusive start and end plain-date interval.
date-range-picker.avoidWhen: Use two independent Date Pickers only when the dates do not form one validated interval.
keyboard: Enter or Space opens the calendar and Escape closes it.
Arrow, Home, End, Page Up, and Page Down move the calendar focus.
Enter or Space selects the start, then the end, while keeping the interval visible.
a11yNotes: The current range phase and selected endpoints are announced.
The calendar exposes grid position, disabled dates, today, and selected endpoints.
The form value uses stable ISO plain dates and rejects an end before the start.
date-range-picker.lifecycleRationale: The two-phase range selection contract remains beta while boundary, locale, and manual assistive-technology evidence are completed.
knownLimitations: Timezone conversion, recurrence, and date-time intervals are outside this component.
Consumers must validate domain-specific inclusivity and unavailable-date rules.

dialog.useWhen: Use Dialog for a focused modal decision or form that must temporarily block interaction with the page.
dialog.avoidWhen: Use Popover for non-modal supplemental content and a route when the task needs durable navigation or deep linking.
keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside the topmost modal surface.
Escape closes the topmost dismissible dialog.
Focus returns to the element that opened the dialog.
a11yNotes: The surface exposes modal dialog semantics with a visible title and optional description.
Initial focus never lands on an inert or hidden element.
Nested overlays register ownership for deterministic Escape and focus restoration.
dialog.lifecycleRationale: The template-owned modal contract remains beta while programmatic opening and complete cross-browser assistive-technology evidence are evaluated.
knownLimitations: There is no public typed imperative overlay service in the current release.
Consumers must verify initial focus and destructive-flow copy for each product dialog.

donut-chart.useWhen: Use Donut Chart for a small part-to-whole composition with clearly distinguishable proportions.
donut-chart.avoidWhen: Use Bar Chart when precise comparison matters or when many small segments would be difficult to distinguish.
keyboard: Tab reaches the source-data toggle and each native legend button.
Focus on a legend button reveals its matching segment and value.
Enter and Space use native button activation; SVG segments do not duplicate tab stops.
a11yNotes: Legend buttons provide the keyboard interaction surface for visual segments.
A semantic source-data table exposes the same labels and values.
Labels and values supplement color and geometry.
donut-chart.lifecycleRationale: The part-to-whole primitive remains beta while legend scale, formatting, and manual assistive-technology evidence mature.
knownLimitations: The primitive is intentionally limited to one series and does not group very small segments.
Consumers must choose a different representation when segment count or similarity impairs comparison.

drawer.useWhen: Use Drawer for a focused modal workflow whose spatial relationship is naturally anchored to a viewport side.
drawer.avoidWhen: Do not use a modal Drawer as permanent application navigation; use Sidebar or Navigation Rail.
keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside the open drawer.
Escape closes the topmost dismissible drawer.
Focus returns to the drawer opener.
a11yNotes: The drawer exposes modal dialog semantics and a visible title.
Logical start/end placement remains correct in LTR and RTL.
Nested overlays preserve deterministic Escape ordering and focus restoration.
drawer.lifecycleRationale: The modal side-surface contract remains beta while placement, nested overlays, and manual assistive-technology evidence are completed.
knownLimitations: There is no public typed imperative overlay service in the current release.
Consumers must verify narrow-layout fallback and safe content width with production forms.

line-chart.useWhen: Use Line Chart for an ordered trend where direction and change over adjacent values are the primary task.
line-chart.avoidWhen: Use Bar Chart for unordered category comparison and a table when exact values dominate.
keyboard: Tab reaches the source-data toggle, then the single roving data mark.
Arrow Left and Arrow Right move between marks and reverse in RTL.
Home and End move to the first and last mark; Enter or Space discloses its value.
a11yNotes: The chart has a specific title and keyboard-operable data marks.
A semantic source-data table exposes the same ordered labels and values.
Focus treatment and value details supplement line geometry and color.
line-chart.lifecycleRationale: The accessible trend primitive remains beta while scale, multi-series direction, and manual assistive-technology evidence mature.
knownLimitations: The primitive does not yet provide multiple series, axes customization, zoom, or large-series virtualization.
Consumers must verify label density and value formatting with production data.

multi-select.useWhen: Use Multi Select when users choose several values from a bounded authoritative option set.
multi-select.avoidWhen: Use Tags Input for user-authored values and Checkbox Group when the complete short option set should stay visible.
keyboard: Enter or Space opens the list; Arrow keys move the active option.
Enter toggles the active option without closing the list.
Escape closes the list and Backspace removes the last token only from an empty query.
a11yNotes: The trigger exposes expansion, list ownership, and active descendant.
Selected values remain visible as named removable tokens.
Loading, empty, error, and selection-count changes are announced.
multi-select.lifecycleRationale: The multi-value popup and token contract remains beta while async option replacement and manual assistive-technology evidence are completed.
knownLimitations: Consumers must keep object option identity stable across refreshes.
Very large selected sets require a product-specific summary or review surface.

resizable-panels.useWhen: Use Resizable Panels when adjacent workspace regions need a persisted user-adjustable size within explicit minimum and maximum bounds.
resizable-panels.avoidWhen: Use Split Layout when regions should follow responsive rules without direct manipulation.
keyboard: Arrow keys adjust the focused separator by the configured step and respect orientation and RTL.
Home and End move to the minimum and maximum allowed size.
Enter or Space toggles the documented collapsed size when collapse is enabled.
a11yNotes: The handle exposes separator orientation, value minimum, maximum, current value, and disabled state.
The separator has an explicit localized accessible name.
Pointer and keyboard changes use the same clamped size model.
resizable-panels.lifecycleRationale: The component is experimental while nested layouts, persistence ownership, touch behavior, and cross-browser accessibility evidence are incubated.
knownLimitations: Consumers own persistence and must reconcile stored size with changed minimum and maximum bounds.
Nested panels and touch resizing require explicit product testing before production adoption.

select.useWhen: Use Select when exactly one value must be chosen from a bounded authoritative option set.
select.avoidWhen: Use Native Select for platform selection, Combobox for searchable options, or Autocomplete for valid free text.
keyboard: Enter or Space opens the list; Arrow keys move the active option.
Enter commits the active option.
Escape closes without changing the committed value.
a11yNotes: The trigger exposes expansion, list ownership, and active descendant.
The selected option label remains the visible source of truth.
Loading, empty, and error states remain perceivable without moving focus.
select.lifecycleRationale: The custom listbox contract remains beta while async states and manual assistive-technology evidence are completed.
knownLimitations: Object values require a stable identityMatcher and trackBy contract.
Consumers must validate long option labels and async error recovery in their layout.

time-picker.useWhen: Use Time Picker for a precise local wall-clock value represented as a 24-hour HH:mm string.
time-picker.avoidWhen: Use a short Select when only a few fixed times are valid, and keep timezone conversion outside the picker.
keyboard: Enter or Space opens the time panel and Escape closes it.
Arrow Up and Arrow Down adjust the focused hour or minute spinbutton.
Enter applies a valid draft time.
a11yNotes: Hour and minute are named spinbuttons with numeric bounds and values.
The formatted draft and validation state remain perceivable.
The form value is a stable 24-hour HH:mm string independent of display copy.
time-picker.lifecycleRationale: The wall-clock editing contract remains beta while locale display and manual assistive-technology evidence are completed.
knownLimitations: Timezone, daylight-saving transitions, dates, and instants are application concerns.
Consumers must validate domain-specific minute increments and unavailable times.

tree.useWhen: Use Tree for hierarchical data that needs roving focus, expansion, selection, and optional asynchronous branches.
tree.avoidWhen: Use Tree Navigation for route wayfinding and nested lists when items do not require composite-widget keyboard behavior.
keyboard: Arrow Up and Arrow Down move through visible enabled nodes.
Arrow Right expands or enters a branch; Arrow Left collapses or returns to its parent.
Home and End jump; typing moves to the next matching visible node.
a11yNotes: Every node id is non-empty, stable, and unique across the complete tree.
Hierarchy, position, expansion, selection, loading, and error states are exposed.
Disabled nodes stay perceivable but are skipped by roving focus.
tree.lifecycleRationale: The hierarchical async-state contract remains beta while large-tree performance and manual assistive-technology evidence are completed.
knownLimitations: Consumers must merge lazy children without creating duplicate ids anywhere in the tree.
Very large trees require consumer performance validation with representative depth and expansion.

tree-navigation.useWhen: Use Tree Navigation for hierarchical route or document wayfinding with expandable branches.
tree-navigation.avoidWhen: Use Tree for selectable domain data and Menu for a short transient action hierarchy.
keyboard: Arrow Up and Arrow Down move through visible enabled items.
Arrow Right expands or enters a branch; Arrow Left collapses or returns to its parent.
Home and End jump; typing moves to the next matching visible item; Enter activates.
a11yNotes: Every navigation item id is non-empty, stable, and unique.
Current location is distinct from focus and selection.
Expansion and hierarchy remain perceivable when labels overflow.
tree-navigation.lifecycleRationale: The hierarchical navigation contract remains beta while router integration patterns and manual assistive-technology evidence are completed.
knownLimitations: Consumers own router authorization, preloading, and failed-navigation feedback.
Deep trees require consumer validation for label overflow and mobile disclosure.
